newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index closes little changed.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index closes little changed.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly lower on Thursday and will likely hover in a tight range in the short term as investors wait for new government cues, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index shed 0.18 points or 0.12 percent to 151.16 as turnover shrank to HK$67.6 million from Wednesday's HK$126.9 million.
"Shenzhen's markets seemed to have steadied as investors take a breather," a trader at a local brokerage said.
"There have been so many rumours (about government moves to cool the markets) in the last month, people do not know what to believe anymore," an analyst at PBI Securities said.
Analysts said the index is unlikely to stray far from current levels, judging from the laggard domestic currency A share index.
The A share index sagged 3.50 points or 0.80 percent to 433.34 on turnover of 5.7 billion yuan, compared with Wednesday's 6.5 billion.
Rumours of government measures to cool the stock markets began to swirl at the start of May, by which time the A and B indices had surged more than 50 percent from the beginning of 1997.
State media said on Thursday that China's central bank had set up two special phone lines for investors to report irregularities and illegal trading on the financial markets.
The move followed a similar annoucement by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) on Wednesday.
"So many rumours are true, some are false and still more are hanging in the air...People are just worn out," an analyst at a foreign investment bank said.
Changchai Co Ltd was the worst performer in the B share market, losing HK$0.48 or 6.26 percent to HK$7.19.
In the A share market, Shenzhen Development Bank fared the worst, plunging 2.88 yuan or 8.02 percent to 33.05 yuan.
Rumours have plagued the bank since it recently failed to hold a scheduled shareholders' meeting due to an investigation into stock trading misconduct, traders said.
